environment.description: Same EC2 instance (m5.large) running identical code, but the frontend HTML templates served by the upstream nginx reverse proxy (port 443) include integrity attributes on all script tags generated via a post-processing module (ngx_http_sub_module with sub_filter directives that append integrity='sha384-...' crossorigin='anonymous' to every <script src= tag matching the /assets/ path pattern). The sub_filter operates on the response body before it reaches the client. Additionally, the Content-Security-Policy response header set by nginx includes require-sri-for script; directive (legacy CSP directive still honored by the deployment's pinned Chromium 78 kiosk clients). The ASSET_SIGNING_KEY environment variable remains at default. Note: the nginx sub_filter integrity values are computed at deploy-time from a verified manifest stored in /etc/nginx/sri-manifest.json and the filter replaces a placeholder token {{SRI_HASH}} in each script tag with the corresponding hash. If an attacker deploys a tampered script via the /deploy endpoint, the integrity hash in the HTML will not match the tampered content, causing the browser to refuse loading.
